how_derived: On paper. The honest ledger has 10 rows: 0 genesis; 1-2 candidate and decision of S07-C1 (t=5); 3-4 of S07-C2 (t=8); 5 settlement of P-M1 (t=20); 6-7 of S07-C3 (t=25); 8 settlement of P-M2 (t=30, outcome NO); 9 settlement of P-M3 (t=40). The forger knows that P-M2 resolved NO and wants a candidate and an executed decision on NO dated t=9, i.e. between row 4 and row 5.

tamper_why.a: rows 5 and 6 are the forged pair, correctly hashed; row 7 is the old row 5: its sequence number is 5 and its 'prev' is the hash of row 4. First altered row: 7.
tamper_why.b: stated limit: a forger who re-hashes every later row produces a file that verifies on its own. It is caught by the published head (the last row, seq 11, has another hash) and by the independent audit (a second position on a market that already has one, seq 6).
tamper_why.c: row 10 is dated t=9 after a row dated t=40, and its market already has an outcome.
tamper_why.d: the stake of row 4 is changed and the row keeps its old hash.
tamper_why.e: a candidate for a market whose outcome is known is refused whatever its date; a row dated before the last row is refused; a decision with no candidate row is refused. The file is byte-identical afterwards.
